newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea probes doctor over video of Kim's son.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea probes doctor over video of Kim's son.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Thursday questioned a doctor whose videotape of President Kim Young-sam's son discussing a top media appointment in his surgery touched off a political storm.
Opposition parties and the media seized on the tape, made public last week, as solid evidence that Kim Hyun-chul meddled in state affairs.

The doctor, Park Kyung-sik, has said he was once close to president Kim's second son but they fell out over business. He said he filmed his patients with their knowledge on a closed-circuit television system.
"The doctor was questioned overnight and released early this morning," a prosecution official, who declined to be identified, said in an interview.

Although an official probe of Hyun-chul had not been launched, the prosecution was investigating suspicions raised by the local press about whether the junior Kim was engaged in influence-peddling, the official said.
The grainy video clip obtained by a citizens' group shows Hyun-chul discussing the appointment of the president of Yonhap Television News.
He was heard mentioning a former minister for the job, which went to another candidate. The minister, Kim Woo-suk, is now in custody after being arrested in a loan scandal.
Yonhap Television is not state owned but its top executives are screened by the government.
The videotape has fuelled attacks by opposition parties, and even some members of the ruling New Korea Party, on Hyun-chul, dubbed by newspapers the "crown prince".

Parliament plans to call the president's son to testify in hearings over a loans scandal involving Hanbo Steel Co, which collapsed in January. A special investigative committee in the National Assembly kicks off its probe on Friday.
Hyun-chul is expected to testify in mid-April and the hearings will be broadcast live.

State prosecutors exonerated him last month after a probe into how Hanbo amassed $5.8 billion in improper loans. But on Monday he apologised, agreed to a new probe and said he was ready for punishment if he had done wrong.
The younger Kim played an important role in his father's election in 1992 but has no position in the administration.
